text:
jen (pm): Thinking out loud — can we add a preflight validator + UI "preview" for runtime config changes that affect routing/quotas? I want to avoid last-minute rollbacks from bad rules.

mattb: yes please. too many manual rollbacks recently. curious how you'd scope it — full eval of traffic impact or just schema + basic sanity checks?

jen (pm): start small: schema + semantic checks (no negative quotas, no cycles in routing), and a lightweight simulator that runs on a sampled traffic profile to show delta on 95p latency and quota spend for 1h/24h. not real traffic.

leo_infra: simulator is ok but expensive. suggestion: sample keys + replay against current routing code in a sandbox w/ cached k/v. we can do traffic-folding for 10% load and extrapolate.

sasha_ui: on the console side, UX needs a clear "what changes" diff and a compact estimation card: expected QPS change, estimated cost delta, and a confidence score. also a snooze/quiet mode for rollout alerts (ops hates noisy canaries).

ruth_ops: snooze is a must. currently every small config tweak floods PagerDuty. would prefer canary window -> if anomaly detected, auto-pause and post to channel.

mattb: implementation notes: add a new internal API endpoint POST /v1/configs/validate that returns {ok, issues[], sim_results_url?}. keep it idempotent and fast (<3s for schema checks, async for simulation).

leo_infra: agree. simulation job should be kicked async and return a presigned link to results. store results for audit. also require a validation webhook option so teams can wire custom checks.

jen (pm): sample patch to console flow:

```
PATCH /console/configs/123/preview
body: {
  "changes": [ {"path": "/routes/route-42/weight", "from": 100, "to": 70 } ],
  "simulate_on": "sampled-10pct"
}
```

sasha_ui: love the preview API. UI should show a tiny flame icon if the change reduces cost but also a warning if latency risk increases. color + microcopy.

ruth_ops: telemetry gating: we need pre/post metric snapshots for sampled keys (token bucket usage, 95p latency, error-rate). Preferably a delta chart with links to traces. Also, retention of these previews for 30d for audits.

mattb: about safety, we should enforce hard caps: validation fails if any route quota < MIN_QUOTA or if total committed GPU load > pool cap. those are quick, deterministic checks. complex heuristics belong in sim.

leo_infra: deployment-wise, we'll run validators as a separate service behind the config API. It will call the router binary in "dry-run" mode inside a containerized sandbox. security: run with least privilege, no access to secrets.

jen (pm): approvals: suggest two modes — quick (team can self-approve with dry-run pass + confidence > 0.8) and formal (requires approver list). Console toggle per-config namespace.

sasha_ui: add an optional "explain" view that highlights which rule caused a simulated increase in latency — map that to the exact route/condition. helps triage.

ruth_ops: plus a playbook link in the preview UI when sim shows regression. automatically attach relevant runbook.

mattb: edge-case: what about concurrent changes? validator should capture base-config version and simulate delta from that exact version; if base changes before promotion, require re-validate. return conflict error code.

leo_infra: also consider a lightweight canary runner — after promotion, apply change to a tiny percent in prod (0.5-1%) with auto-escalate if thresholds hit. integrate with current rollout service.

jen (pm): timeline proposal: M1: schema + static checks + console diff. M2: async sim + results link + retention. M3: approval flows + webhook + auto-canary integration.

sasha_ui: will sketch mocks for M1 (diff + estimation card) tomorrow.

ruth_ops: I'll draft the alert-snooze & auto-pause rules for canary step.

mattb: I'll add api contract PR for /validate and async job. putting up an implementation spike next week.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: config-validator/spike -> dev cluster on 2026-03-28T03:00Z :rocket:

jen (pm): thanks all — assigning tasks in the thread. we'll iterate based on spike findings. :thumbsup:
